exceptions.justification: @socketsecurity/cli is only a link in the dependency path to zod, which carries advisory GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 (memory exhaustion when validating oversized constrained collections, <4.6.6). The path is @socketsecurity/cli -> @socketsecurity/socket-patch -> zod@3.25.76; the SecuritySocket check runs the CLI.
exceptions.alternatives: Drop the SecuritySocket check, which every package relies on for its supply-chain gate; or override zod under socket-patch and accept untested behaviour in the tool that guards releases.
exceptions.attempted: Ran `npm audit fix` and `npm update`, and checked for a newer release of each package in the path; @socketsecurity/cli 1.10.1 is the latest published, and its newest @socketsecurity/socket-patch (5.0.1) still pins zod 3.25.76. The only fix npm offers is a downgrade of @socketsecurity/cli to 1.1.66.
exceptions.constraint: @socketsecurity/socket-patch depends on zod 3.25.76 exactly, and zod 4.6.6 (the first patched release) is a different major version whose API socket-patch has not adopted; overriding it would run Socket's code against an API it was not written for.
exceptions.remediation: Upgrade as soon as socket-patch accepts a patched zod; Dependabot will propose the @socketsecurity/cli update.
exceptions.residualRisk: Exploiting it needs an attacker to control a very large collection that zod validates inside socket-patch. It validates Socket's own patch metadata inside the check run in CI or on a developer machine, never in a service handling untrusted requests.
exceptions.revisitWhen: @socketsecurity/socket-patch moves to zod 4.6.6 or later, or Socket publishes a CLI that drops it.
exceptions.ruleBroken: SecurityDeps: no unresolved high-severity npm audit finding in what the package installs.
exceptions.whyPreferable: Dropping the Socket gate would remove supply-chain scanning from every package; the exposure below needs attacker-controlled input to a schema, which socket-patch does not take from untrusted sources.
